Which Markets Really Declined?

MediumFreeQuerying BasicsConditional LogicAggregation & GroupingSubqueries & CTEs

February revenue fell in three countries, and the regional lead wants to know which of those are a real decline and which are a change in what people bought. A market really declined when both revenue and units fell by more than 5% from January to February 2024. Revenue down while units go up means people bought cheaper items, not fewer of them.

Use completed orders only. Show exactly these 8 columns: country, jan_revenue and feb_revenue (sum of total, rounded to 2 decimals), revenue_change_pct (rounded to 1 decimal), jan_units and feb_units (sum of quantity), units_change_pct (1 decimal) and real_decline (1 or 0). Order by country.

Solve it in the browser editor →

Runs on SQLite in your browser, graded against the expected result, no signup. A wrong answer gets a diagnosis, not just "incorrect". Free accounts get 10 free challenge solves, and this can be one of them.

11Laptop ProElectronics11299.991299.992024-01-15USAcompleted
22Wireless MouseElectronics249.9999.982024-01-16Canadacompleted
33Office ChairFurniture1349.99349.992024-01-17USAcompleted

Expected output: 7 rows — UK: revenue 639.98 → 49.99 (−92.2%), units 2 → 1 (−50.0%), real_decline 1; USA: revenue −41.9% but units +83.3%, real_decline 0

Hint

Put a country's two months side by side on one row first, with the month test inside each sum. The change is (February − January) / January × 100; multiply by 100.0 rather than 100, or whole-number units divide down to 0. A real decline needs both changes below −5%.
